text:
julie han: heads up — scorecard alert spam starting ~07:30 UTC, looks correlated with runner v2.3.1 deploy :grimacing:
omar r: seeing it too. lots of tiny +100%-500% deltas on 'prompt-quality' in the daily timeseries :eyes:
nik patel: do we have a hypothesis? the raw evals for the same runs look fine locally
julie han: quick debug — plotted raw counts and noticed the aggregation window shifted from 1h -> 1m for some series. suspecting smoothing/rollup mismatch when we compute baseline
kai chen: that would blow up pct deltas if denominator went to near-zero. which component applies the smoothing?
nik patel: it's the frontend timeseries pipeline: we run a rolling_mean(window=5) then aggregate_by_hour. I think the order got swapped in the new optimize PR 482
julie han: repro snippet I used:
```python
# simplified
series = get_series('prompt-quality', start, end)
smoothed = series.rolling(5).mean()  # currently applied BEFORE hourly_resample
agg = smoothed.resample('1H').mean()
# expected: resample first, then rolling smoothing inside each hour
```
omar r: ah — PR 482 changes aggregator order to reduce tail-lag. unit tests missed the case where series has many zero-count buckets
kai chen: adding: when count is zero, rolling mean can return NaN which got treated as 0 in the diffing job, producing huge % increases when later nonzero appears
julie han: eval-bot: alert stream attached for context -> :point_down:
eval-bot: [alert id: A-2026-03-20-17] 37 alerts fired for metric prompt-quality, median delta 320%
nik patel: quick mitigation options: 1) revert PR 482 2) patch pipeline to resample before rolling 3) change diff job to use absolute deltas when denominator < 1
kai chen: prefer patch 2 + 3. revert has rollbacks pain, and we should fix diff logic anyway
omar r: agree. i'll open a hotfix PR to reorder ops and add guard in diff calc. putting up a deploy target for canary region only
julie han: also need a retroactive recalculation for the alert window — otherwise on-call will chase ghosts. can we re-run rollups for the last 24h?
nik patel: yes, I'll schedule a backfill job. command I'll run:
```bash
python infra/run_backfill.py --metric prompt-quality --from -24h --to now --force-recompute
```
kai chen: add a note to alerts: "possible smoothing order bug" so pagers know it's tooling not model regression
omar r: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/489 — patch + tests. test covers zero-count buckets and NaN propagation
julie han: thanks. once canary looks good, promote and reindex alerts. also update the runbook with the check for resample vs rolling
nik patel: opened issue #1024 for runbook and postmortem checklist
kai chen: small follow-up — the diff view in console also computes relative pct using baseline_mean instead of baseline_sum which caused some percentages >1000% for top-k metrics. i'll audit calc in ui diff component
julie han: good catch. can you add that to PR or a separate PR?
kai chen: separate tiny PR incoming
omar r: deploying canary now. will post logs in 15m :hourglass_flowing_sand:
julie han: :thumbsup: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turnaround. will update the channel after backfill completes
nik patel: backfill kicked, ETA ~12m
eval-bot: alert resolved: A-2026-03-20-17 (after backfill and hotfix)
